title: "Method B: Magnitude-Invariant Entropy"
---

# 🧠 Theoretical Framework

Standard protection relays fail in IBR-dominated microgrids because control loops mask fault magnitudes. **Method B** analyzes the **informational chaos** (entropy) of the current waveform, ensuring detection even when the inverter limits fault current to $1.1 \text{ pu}$.

---

### 🔬 Mathematical Foundation

We define the probability $p_i$ of a current sample falling into a specific quantization bin $i$:

$$p_i = \frac{n_i}{N}$$

The **Shannon Entropy** ($H$) is calculated as:

$$H = -\sum_{i=1}^{K} p_i \ln(p_i)$$

To achieve **Magnitude-Invariance**, we normalize against the maximum possible uncertainty ($\ln K$):

$$H_{norm} = \frac{-\sum p_i \ln(p_i)}{\ln(K)}$$

**Result:** * $H_{norm} \approx 0$: Pure sinusoidal/steady state.
* $H_{norm} \to 1$: High-Impedance Fault (HIF) or Inverter Control Interaction (Chaos).
